history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE PAIR: seq 1179 'Debi Chaudhurani Mandir' (id debi-chaudhurani-mandir-jalpaiguri) is the same shrine — identical coordinates; keep-or-merge decision needed. IDENTITY UNCERTAIN: no independent web footprint exists for a 'Maa Bhabani Temple' in Jalpaiguri; this entry provisionally documents the Devi Chaudhurani (Bhabani Pathak) Kali shrine near Goshala More/Falakata Road, Jalpaiguri town, since 'Bhabani' refers to Bhabani Pathak, the Sannyasi-rebellion leader and mentor of the 'bandit queen' Devi Chaudhurani (Jayadurga Devi, zamindar of Manthana/Pirgacha, 1765-1801), heroine of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's 1884 novel Devi Chaudhurani. Local legend holds that Devi Chaudhurani established a Kali temple near Goshala More; its Kali Puja still draws hundreds. A separate 250-year-old Devi Choudhurani temple at Shikarpur Tea Estate, Belakoba (~18 km away) was restored by the West Bengal government and may be a distinct site with the same name - the two should not be conflated. Coordinates are for the town temple as geocoded.

name: Maa Bhabani Temple
town_description: Jalpaiguri is the divisional headquarters of North Bengal, set between the Teesta and Karala rivers. Once the seat of the Raikat rulers of Baikunthapur, it is the gateway to the Dooars and is ringed by tea gardens, the Baikunthapur forest and colonial-era buildings.

travel.airport: Bagdogra International Airport (IXB), about 60 km away, is the nearest airport; taxis and buses connect it to Jalpaiguri.
travel.railway: Jalpaiguri and Jalpaiguri Road stations are a few km away; New Jalpaiguri (NJP), the main junction, is about 45 km away.
travel.road: On Falakata Road near Goshala More in Jalpaiguri town, reachable by auto-rickshaw or taxi.

visitor_information.best_time: October-November for Kali Puja/Diwali; November-February is climatically pleasant.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Hours not published online; typically open morning and evening like other Kali temples (verify).
